solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Belittle bridge opponents with "mug to lead"

indicators.note: the mug goes in front of the bridge players

parts.note: a mug is a fool, and so is a dodo
West and North sit in opposing partnerships at bridge

explanation.surface: A bridge player sneers at the opponents, putting the table's fool in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: At bridge North partners South and East partners West, so any two neighbouring seats, such as W and N, are opponents.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean to disparage someone, make them seem small.

clue.text: Fine curtailed Trump's flakiness?

definitions.note: Flakiness is the condition; dandruff is the flakes themselves.

indicators.note: cut off at the tail: the last letter goes

parts.note: to ruff is to play a trump card

explanation.surface: A jibe at a certain politician's unreliable temperament.
explanation.walkthrough: Trump's capital letter points at the politician; it is the card-game verb. The question mark flags the playful definition: dandruff is literally flakiness of the scalp.
explanation.definitionFit: Dandruff is flakes of dead skin, so a flaky condition, stretched here with a question mark.

clue.text: Trail broken leg, bearing pain

indicators.note: the letters of LEG are broken up and rearranged
in a down clue the leg sits below and bears the pain on top of it

parts.note: a drag is a pain, a tiresome thing

explanation.surface: An injured walker limps along a path with a broken leg, in pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trail' looks like a footpath noun; it is the verb. 'Bearing' works because this is a down clue: the broken leg sits underneath the pain, holding it up.
explanation.definitionFit: To draggle is to trail along behind, or through mud.

clue.text: Popular Liberal upset butcher in garden

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the word upside down, reversing it

parts.note: first half of WEED, to garden

indicators.note: the Liberal and reversed butcher go inside the garden verb

explanation.surface: A well-loved Liberal politician is toppled by a slaughterer in someone's garden.
explanation.walkthrough: Garden and butcher both look like nouns; both are verbs here, to weed and to kill. L plus LLIK makes three L's in a row, which is why the hyphen helps.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe someone whom many people like.

clue.text: Called again about faulty gadget

indicators.note: the gadget's letters are faulty, so out of order

explanation.surface: Someone phones the helpline a second time about a broken gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Called' suggests a phone call; it means named, as a tag names something.
explanation.definitionFit: To tag something is to label or name it, so retagged is renamed, called again.

clue.text: Actor and journalist on identical charges having pinched fuel

indicators.note: in a down clue the journalist sits on top of what follows
the two charges have stolen the fuel and hold it between them

parts.note: a ward is someone in another's charge

explanation.surface: A news story: an actor and a reporter face the same charges for stealing fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward Woodward was an English actor, star of The Equalizer and The Wicker Man. 'Charges' suggests criminal counts; here they are people in someone's care.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Woodward was a well-known English actor.

clue.text: Casual job rejected by great old buffoon

indicators.note: the casual job is thrown out of the bigger word

parts.note: a gig is a one-off piece of work, removed from the front

explanation.surface: A pompous old fool turns down some casual work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Great old' reads as a phrase, but the break comes after 'great': 'old' belongs to the definition, since ANTIC in this sense is archaic.
explanation.definitionFit: An antic was once a clown or grotesque performer, a buffoon.

clue.text: Coaching failed to yield first-class dumplings

indicators.note: the coaching went wrong, so its letters are scrambled
to yield is to surrender something, so the first-class A is handed over and dropped

parts.note: the anagram fodder before the loss
A = first-class, as in A1; this letter is removed

explanation.surface: Bad cooking lessons meant nobody turned out top-quality dumplings.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a cookery class that went wrong, and gnocchi is exactly what such a class might attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: these Italian potato morsels are one kind of dumpling.

clue.text: Increase strength of hideaway, covering leak up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read bottom to top
the hideaway wraps around the leak

parts.note: a den is a hideaway, split around the leak
PEE (slang for a leak, urinating) reversed

explanation.surface: Advice to reinforce a secret shelter by covering a leak in its roof.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leak' is British slang for urinating, as in 'take a leak', so it gives PEE.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: making a colour, feeling or sound more intense strengthens it.

clue.text: Enter bar in felt buckles? That's an embarrassment

definitions.note: The definition names the effect; the answer is the person who causes it.

indicators.note: the phrase buckles out of shape, rearranging its letters

explanation.surface: Someone walks into a pub wearing felt shoes with buckles and is mocked for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buckles' looks like a noun, fasteners on felt shoes; it is the verb, to bend out of shape.
explanation.definitionFit: An enfant terrible is someone whose outrageous behaviour embarrasses their associates.

clue.text: Criminal lawyer and con man spoke at last in good nick

indicators.note: the lawyer's letters are crooked, so rearranged
take the final letter of each of the next words

parts.note: last letters of coN, maN, spokE

explanation.surface: A crooked lawyer and a swindler are finally caught and talk in the police station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal lawyer' reads as one job title; 'criminal' is the anagram indicator. 'In good nick' is British for in good condition, while 'nick' also means a police station.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nearly new has hardly been used, so it is in good condition.

clue.text: Outgoing type stripped twice in store

indicators.note: strip off the outer letters, then do it again

parts.note: an extrovert is an outgoing person

explanation.surface: An extrovert goes wild and undresses in a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Store' suggests a shop; it means a hoard, as in treasure trove.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of a hoard or cache of valuables.

clue.text: Bring back one beer to accompany a big cigar

indicators.note: the whole string is turned round
the one and the beer go alongside the A

explanation.surface: An order at the bar: bring me a beer to go with my big cigar.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a drinks order, and the cigar belongs in it. Regalia is less familiar as a cigar size than as royal insignia.
explanation.definitionFit: A regalia is a large, high-quality cigar.

clue.text: Seek further use for components within grey vehicle

indicators.note: take the letters found inside the word, dropping its outer ones

explanation.surface: Advice on salvaging parts from an old grey car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Components' reads as car parts to be salvaged; it points to the inner letters of 'grey'.
explanation.definitionFit: A paraphrase: processing waste or old goods so they can be used again.

clue.text: Spot sheep collectively shifting over to middle of field

indicators.note: one letter changes into another

parts.note: a flock is a group of sheep
O = over, from cricket scoring; this letter is replaced

explanation.surface: A farmer notices the flock drifting over to the centre of the field.
explanation.walkthrough: O for over comes from cricket scorecards. The surface is a pastoral scene, and the sheep really do move into the field.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a tiny mark or speck of colour.

clue.text: Community has charging point finally switched on

indicators.note: take only the last letter

explanation.surface: A village announces that its new electric-car charger is now live.
explanation.walkthrough: The T goes before OWNS even though 'has' comes first in the clue. 'Switched on' looks like the charger working; it means trendy and alert.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym; in South Africa the word also named an area set aside for Black residents under apartheid.

clue.text: Complaint papers raised ulcer acquired by relative

indicators.note: the relative takes the other pieces inside it

parts.note: first letter of SIS, a sister

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means written upwards, reversed

explanation.surface: A newspaper runs a complaint about an ulcer a relative caught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complaint' looks like a grievance sent to the papers; it is a medical complaint, an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Siderosis is a lung disease caused by inhaling iron dust, so a complaint in the medical sense.

clue.text: One's inclined to bend the limits of radioisotope dating

indicators.note: bend the letters out of order
only the outer letters of radioisotope are used

parts.note: first and last letters of RadioisotopE

explanation.surface: A scientist admits to pushing the limits of carbon dating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Radioisotope dating' reads as one technical term; only the ends of the first word and all of the second are needed.
explanation.definitionFit: A slope is literally something inclined, and the 's plays on a person being inclined to do something.

clue.text: City hospital to decline work

parts.note: to die away is to decline
a machine that goes is working

explanation.surface: A city hospital is going downhill, turning away work.
explanation.walkthrough: SAN, short for sanatorium, is a school-and-crossword word for a hospital or sickbay.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a large port city in southern California.

clue.text: Pile of workers want to go topless — Benny, for example

indicators.note: in a down clue the top is the first letter, which goes

explanation.surface: A cheeky comedy sketch in which Benny Hill wants to strip off.
explanation.walkthrough: Benny Hill was a British TV comedian known for saucy slapstick, which is why going topless suits the surface. 'Workers' are ants, as so often.
explanation.definitionFit: An anthill is a heap built by worker ants.

clue.text: Writer's miserable doctor tried, having neglected case

indicators.note: the outer letters, the case of the word, are left off

parts.note: HEARD (tried, as a court hears a case) without H…D

explanation.surface: An author is gloomy because the doctor tried to treat him but ignored his case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer's' marks drear as a literary word rather than everyday speech. 'Case' has a double life: a medical case in the surface, the outside letters in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Drear is a poetic form of dreary, miserable.

clue.text: Loner's suitable moment to return, before crowds

indicators.note: the word for before crowds round the reversed moment
the moment is sent back, reversed

explanation.surface: A recluse judges the right time to come back ahead of the crowds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crowds' looks like a noun, the throngs a loner avoids; it is a verb, squeezing round something. The 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an archaic word for a hermit, a religious recluse.

clue.text: Beautiful actions excuse turning up now and then

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means reversing
something done now and then happens only intermittently, so only every other letter is taken

parts.note: every second letter of aCtIoNs ExCuSe

explanation.surface: Graceful moves that excuse showing up only occasionally.
explanation.walkthrough: Of the alternate-letter sets, only the even ones spell anything backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A near synonym, used of views and landscapes that are beautiful to look at.

clue.text: Drained theatre nurse maybe collars food supplier

indicators.note: the nurse grabs the drained theatre and holds it

parts.note: a nurse is one kind of carer

indicators.note: emptied of its insides, leaving the outer letters

explanation.surface: An exhausted theatre nurse grabs the man supplying the food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Theatre nurse' reads as an operating-theatre job; the phrase splits.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain description: the firm or person who provides food and drink for events.

clue.text: Partly lifting ottoman is ordinarily a help when varnishing

indicators.note: the answer is part of the words that follow
in a down clue, lifting means read upwards

explanation.surface: Advice that lifting the ottoman usually helps when you are varnishing the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: The furniture-moving surface hides a tree resin that goes into varnish.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosin is a resin used in making varnishes.

clue.text: Revolutionary Green leader? That could be incendiary

indicators.note: turned right round, reversed

explanation.surface: A radical Green Party leader is branded a firebrand.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital G makes 'Green' look political; it is green meaning raw, inexperienced.
explanation.definitionFit: A warhead is the explosive tip of a missile, and some are incendiary.

clue.text: Catches slowcoach delaying son's appearance

parts.note: SNAIL (a slowcoach) with its S taken out
S = son, now appearing at the end

explanation.surface: A late-running boy holds up everyone waiting for him.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of SNAIL is not lost, only delayed: it moves from the front to the back.
explanation.definitionFit: To nail someone is to catch them.

clue.text: Fools lease land west of London

parts.note: berk is British slang for a fool

explanation.surface: Some foolish people rent a plot of land outside London.
explanation.walkthrough: Berkshire is an English county west of London. Berk is mild British slang for an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by description: the English county lying just west of Greater London.

clue.text: Solid shelf delivered with fashionable red backing

indicators.note: the red is written backwards
spoken, as a speech is delivered

parts.note: a sill is a shelf; said out loud it matches CYL

explanation.surface: A sturdy shelf arrives with a trendy red back panel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solid' looks like an adjective describing the shelf; it is the noun, a geometric solid.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: in geometry a solid is a three-dimensional shape, and this is one.

clue.text: Act like court has sealed the end for MS Outlook

indicators.note: the imitation and court close round the letter
the end of MS is its final letter

parts.note: last letter of MS, sealed after the A

explanation.surface: A court seals the fate of Microsoft's email program.
explanation.walkthrough: 'MS Outlook' reads as the Microsoft product, but the phrase splits: MS supplies S and Outlook is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspect is an outlook or view, as a south-facing aspect.
